descriptionAdvanced.en: The Uyuni Railway Station is a historic and atmospheric landmark that has been the lifeblood of the city since its founding in 1889. It serves as the most important junction of the Western Railway (FCA), connecting the Altiplano with the cities of Oruro and Villazón, and the international routes to Chile and Argentina. Historically, the station was the vital link for the export of Bolivia's mineral wealth during the tin and silver eras. Today, while freight transport remains important, the station is world-famous as the arrival point for thousands of international tourists who come to explore the Salar de Uyuni. The sight of vintage train cars against the stark Altiplano landscape creates a unique sense of nostalgia and provides a tangible connection to Bolivia's industrial past.

en: The station is the headquarters of the Ferroviaria Andina (FCA) operations in the southern region.
It is famous for the 'Expreso del Sur' and 'Wara Wara del Sur' passenger trains that run to the Argentine border.
The station area includes historic workshops and the nearby Train Cemetery, which is a major tourist attraction.
It is located at an altitude of 3,670 meters, making it one of the highest functional railway hubs in the world.
